questions.question: What is the quickest way to start a new Next.js project with the recommended defaults?
options: npm install react and write a webpack config by hand
Download a zip of the Next.js source code
npm run build in an empty folder
questions.explanation: create-next-app scaffolds the project and installs dependencies; --yes accepts the recommended defaults (TypeScript, ESLint, Tailwind, App Router, Turbopack).

questions.question: You create the file app/contact/page.tsx. Which URL serves it?
questions.explanation: In the App Router, folders become URL segments and page.tsx makes the segment publicly reachable, so app/contact/page.tsx is served at /contact.

questions.question: You changed a page, but `npm run start` still shows the old version. Why?
options: Production mode serves the last build and does not watch files, so you must run npm run build again
Fast Refresh is broken and Node.js must be reinstalled
npm run start only works with JavaScript, not TypeScript
The browser cache must be cleared every time
questions.explanation: next start serves the output in .next/ from the last next build. Only next dev watches files and applies Fast Refresh.

questions.question: What is the minimum Node.js version recent Next.js releases require?
questions.explanation: The lesson notes that recent versions of Next.js need Node.js 20.9 or newer; check with node --version.
